marta: Heads up 9 4a1 were seeing late-token hallucination spikes on long-context when requests with mixed quant (FP8/INT8/4bit) land in the same batch. Low-hanging theory: kv hits get polluted when slices with different quant representations share cache slots. Short thread to decide next step.
chris: Which customer signals? any concrete deltas?
marta: Two signals: (1) deg-rate on production evals jumps ~8-12% on long prompts, (2) users report truncated/fuzzy end-of-output. Correlates with "mixed-bit batch" scheduling logs.
li: Can you paste an anonymized scheduling sample?
marta: ```
SCHED ts=6291234550 id=0x7f bits=[fp8,4bit,fp8] avg_seq=1800 kv_miss=0.41 tail_delta=0.16
SCHED ts=6291234560 id=0x80 bits=[fp8,fp8,fp8] avg_seq=300 kv_miss=0.92 tail_delta=0.01
```
diego: If kv entries are typed by raw bytes, mixing quant reps could cause deserialization mismatch or evictions because sizes differ. Two quick ideas: (A) bit-fenced KV buckets (each quant has separate namespace) or (B) per-request "precision-tag" that forces run-time to avoid co-packing incompatible slices.
chris: Option A adds memory overhead but is simpler to reason about. Option B keeps packing density but increases scheduler complexity.
li: We should empiricalize. Small experiments: (1) bit-fencing for 5% traffic, (2) priority pinning for customers with spike history for 10 min windows, (3) shadow replays that reproduce exact mixed/mono-bit batches.
canary-bot: Canary created: bit-fence-sample job 5% traffic starting 6291234600. Reports to #eng-ml-canaries.
diego: Telemetry tweak needed: add fields "precision_tag", "kv_namespace", "kv_entry_size", "batch_bits_order", and "tail_delta" to per-request trace. Also capture a compact "prompt_fingerprint" for replayability.
marta: Agree. Also add a lightweight "pack_loss" boolean when a scheduled batch reduced kv hit below threshold.
chris: Tradeoffs: fencing will reduce cross-bit packing ratio. Need to estimate token/sec delta on high-throughput endpoints. Suggest microbench: simulate 1k rps with mixed bit distribution and measure throughput for fenced vs packed.
li: For replays we need deterministic KV priming. Plan: capture (model_sha, prompt_fingerprint, seed, initial_kv_digest, batch_bits_order). Provide helper to reconstruct initial_kv_digest from shadow agent.
diego: Action items: marta + chris do microbench and short PR for scheduler flags; li drafts telemetry proto and shadow-replay harness; ops runs 5% canary and surface per-bit deg + latency.
marta: Will open PR and attach microbench graphs. Ping @li for telemetry proto review. :eyes:
